Shown when the same save changed on two devices. Two cards, one per copy, carry the device, the time and which is newer; the person keeps this device's copy, the other one, or both when a slot is free.

## In each kit

<Tabs syncKey="ui-kit">
  <TabItem label="React">
    <KitStatus kit="react" />

    **Drop-in.** `<SaveConflict />` from `@polaris-key/react/kit`, inside `<PolarisKeyProvider config={polarisKey}>`. It follows the first open MergeRequest of the saves collection and answers it with `request.keep`; the client holds this device's copy, so there is no `bytes` prop. With no conflict it draws nothing. A conflict that appears after a save takes focus once. Cancel keeps the conflict pending; the [Cloud Sync strip](/docs/build/ui/components/cloud-sync-status/) keeps asking, and Review opens the screen again.

    **Cards.** Every SDK stores `savedAt` (milliseconds) and `deviceLabel` (the device's display name, never a hardware value) in the metadata of each save, and the cards read them. Your own `savedAt` or `deviceLabel` key is overwritten. `when` defaults to the platform's medium date and time of `savedAt`. `describe` is optional and overrides a card's `when`, `device` or `newer`.

    **Styled part and headless.** Given an `input.saveConflict` it is the plain part and the host drives it; `viewOf("SaveConflict", input)` returns the view.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="SwiftUI">
    <KitStatus kit="swiftui" />

    **Styled part.** `SaveConflictView(model:)` over `SaveConflictModel(request:)`, from `PolarisKeyUI` and `PolarisKeyUICore`. The model reads both copies, `bothAvailable` and `newer` from the `MergeRequest` and applies a choice with `request.keep`, so the app passes no bytes. `SaveConflictModel(conflict:inputs:host:)` is the plain form, with `SaveConflictHost(keep:)`, one closure that throws when it could not apply the choice. `onKept`, `onCancel`, `onChooseAgain` and `onDone` on the model tell you where the person went.

    ```swift

import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import PolarisKeyUICore
import SwiftUI

@MainActor
func saveConflictScreen(request: MergeRequest) -> some View {
SaveConflictView(model: SaveConflictModel(request: request))
}

```

    **Headless.** `KitStates.saveConflict(_:)`. [SwiftUI](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/swiftui/) has the theme and the restyle hooks.

  </TabItem>
